note: ADR-0069 regression capture, extended by ADR-0074 with a fourth node. Two fixture-free bypass denials fail because the ancestor returns ALLOW; the positive control and the consumed-slot exclusion node fail because the ancestor requires caller-supplied args.slot_id instead of deriving and consuming the matching slot. Fixture setup completes before every property assertion. SCOPE OF THE F-1 CLAIM (ADR-0074 decision 2, verbatim): "F-1 makes a consumed slot a derivation candidate; the observable consequence is a false ambiguity denial on the index-sanctioned reuse path, asserted on persisted worker_slots columns. F-1 cannot produce a duplicate dispatch: the one-use compare-and-set independently forecloses it." The kill is on the LIVENESS face, not the safety face; a reviewer who expects "the mutant lets a bad dispatch through" is right to reject that framing, because no such scenario exists. Additionally: at ancestor 6b52252 the new node fails at its FIRST assertion for the same reason the existing positive control does (args.slot_id required), so it contributes a MUTATION KILL AT HEAD, NOT INDEPENDENT ANCESTOR REGRESSION EVIDENCE.

capture.composition: HYBRID TREE. This is a genuine hybrid and always will be: RT-16's regression evidence is only meaningful against an ancestor policy module, so the tests, the CLI and every other file come from the test SHA while exactly one file comes from the baseline SHA. staff finding F-8 exists because that composition was previously unrecorded.

All four bound nodes are present in tests/test_admission_derivation.py at this SHA, and that file is byte-identical here and at the branch head, so the capture is reproducible from this immutable id alone. It moved from 5b1d39fbe18de70b3d21e80021cf705b6b072d83 (the commit that introduced node 4) because `unittest -v` echoes each test's docstring first line, so the renumber changed this capture's own recorded output -- leaving the old SHA would hand a reader pre-renumber docstrings against a post-renumber capture. reproduce: cd /tmp/rt16anc/tests && python3 -m unittest -v <the four node ids in `command` above>

capture.trap_o_nofollow: The CURRENT deploy/policies/omnipods_policies.py calls _load_attested_controller() at import time, opening Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]/bin/nightshift-ctl with O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOFOLLOW. A symlinked bin/nightshift-ctl, or a bare directory holding only the policy file, therefore fails with "ImportError: cannot open admission controller: <path>" before any test runs. The 6b52252 policy has NO such loader (it imports only os, re, sqlite3, time), so swapping TO the ancestor works -- but only inside a full repo-shaped tree with a real bin/nightshift-ctl file. Swapping the other way, or symlinking, does not.
capture.setup_failure_discriminator: unittest reports a property miss as a FAILURE and a setUp/import/loader/CLI-init/fixture collapse as an ERROR. This capture must show failures=4, errors=0, and its text must contain no 'in setUp', 'ImportError', 'ModuleNotFoundError', 'AttributeError: module', or '_FailedTest' occurrence. Verified on capture: none present. The third and fourth nodes' recorded reasons are the ancestor evaluator's own args.slot_id refusal, which is itself proof that the database and CLI fixture completed before the policy was consulted.

negative_control.what: Running baseline_sha + command with NO swap -- i.e. a PURE 6b52252 checkout, which is what a reader who takes the two recorded fields at face value would do.
negative_control.command: git worktree add --detach /tmp/pure6b 6b52252ff8c4975ffc30a59b3142ae6b86a90875 && cd /tmp/pure6b/tests && python3 -m unittest -v <the four node ids above>
negative_control.measured: FAILED (errors=4), exit 1. ImportError / ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'test_admission_derivation' -- the file does not exist at 6b52252 at all. testsRun=4, failures=0, errors=4.
negative_control.why_it_matters: Same exit code (1) as the real capture, for an entirely different reason: nothing was tested. This is precisely staff finding F-8's point, and it is why the swap procedure above is load-bearing rather than incidental. The FAILURE-vs-ERROR counters separate the two unambiguously: the real capture is failures=4/errors=0, this one is failures=0/errors=4. A reviewer re-running the bare (baseline_sha, command) pair and seeing exit 1 must not read that as corroboration.
negative_control.note_on_the_spec: docs/specs/506-step2-manifest-binding.md item 5 criterion 3 describes this negative control as reproducing 'exit 1, failures=3' with the third failure in setUp ('AssertionError: 2 != 0', the ancestor CLI rejecting today's argv). That is not what this file/SHA pair produces -- tests/test_admission_derivation.py was added long after 6b52252, so the module cannot even be imported and no test body runs. The measurement above is recorded in preference to the spec's description; flagged to pm.

mutations.rationale: Issue #608. A consumed slot must never be re-derived. Under this mutant the index-sanctioned identity-reuse path becomes a two-row `ambiguous dispatch identity` denial, which the fourth node detects on persisted worker_slots columns with no dependence on any reason string (issue #607).
mutations.observed: FAILED (failures=2): the pre-existing positive control (via its reason-string assertion) and the new consumed-slot exclusion node (via `second['result']` and its persisted-state assertions). The two fixture-free bypass nodes are unaffected, as expected.
mutations.not_validated_by_dod_validate: RT-16 is a `regression`-kind record, and tests/dod_validate.py's validate_rt_baseline only invokes _validate_mutation when derived_kind == 'preservation'. This mutations array is therefore audit evidence for #608 and is NOT mechanically checked by the validator; it does not gate D06's flip. Claim no validator coverage for it.
